image_description: An underwater close-up shot of a large cetacean, specifically focusing on the head and anterior body. The animal exhibits dark, mottled grey skin covered in white speckles (barnacles/lice). A broad pectoral flipper is visible extending from the side, and the rostrum appears arched. The lighting is dim, typical of deep water, with some particulate matter suspended in the blue-green background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is cropped tightly on the side of the head; the top of the rostrum and blowholes are outside the frame or obscured by the angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture clearly shows the characteristic mottling and white cyamid/barnacle patches associated with grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image only shows the anterior section of the whale; the dorsal region is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body appears massive and robust, consistent with the scale of a baleen whale.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint; the body skin matches the description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed or the angle does not reveal the interior oral cavity where baleen plates would be located.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large, broad pectoral flipper is clearly visible in the lower-left quadrant, matching the anatomical description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The high-resolution texture of the skin shows the roughness and callosities expected of this species.
